question.problem:
Find the binormal vector to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $t=2$, given that

$$
\begin{aligned}T(2) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨0,1,2⟩, \\ N(2) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨0,2,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
The binormal vector is given by

$$
B(t)=T(t)\times N(t).
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B(2) & =T(2)\times N(2) \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨0,1,2⟩\times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}⟨0,2,-1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨(-1-4),-(0-0),(0-0)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨-5,0,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
